title: Choose the decision-desk composition
question: Light and dark will both ship. Choose the information hierarchy that should govern both modes.

options.label: Move Tree First
options.thesis: The weekly candidate table leads, with future impact explained as a right-side continuation and a full-width season move tree.
options.viewport: The weekly decision owns the center; a compact future-impact panel and branching season line complete the explanation.
options.risk: The ensemble forecast chart would have to enter below the fold or replace some of the right-side explanation.

options.label: Balanced Horizon
options.thesis: Candidate comparison and the forecast horizon share the first viewport, while the season move tree remains continuous below them.
options.viewport: A roughly even split keeps this week’s choice actionable while showing the probabilistic future consequence beside it.
options.risk: It carries the most simultaneous information and depends on disciplined responsive collapse on smaller screens.

options.label: Ensemble Focus
options.thesis: A compact decision column leaves the season forecast as the dominant analytical instrument, with the move tree and impact audit below.
options.viewport: The chart receives most of the horizontal field; the weekly choice remains fixed and actionable at left.
options.risk: The chart can feel more authoritative than the underlying model warrants unless uncertainty and assumptions stay explicit.
